question: Would learned probabilities help when restricted to the components and remaining budget of a single real autonomous run, as opposed to combining evidence from multiple development runs?
source: Use the existing matched-finalist run, the two prospective frontier runs, the ordinary higher-budget portfolio, and the existing anonymous non-H2 development image. Each case is evaluated from its own previously frozen finalist plan. Incomplete or single-confirmation evidence is reported as ineligible. No designated validation or external image outcomes.
fit: Fit one shrinkage-to-uniform simplex Brier vote on the primary training fold for all the individual components that the agent itself committed to checking. If more than three components, retain the three largest weights and refit once. Compare its untouched weights to the actual deployed recipe and its own equal-weight version on both later disjoint training folds. Keep actual row and label alignment throughout. Charge actual optimizer fits separately and account for replacing the deployed components' refits.
decision: A case warrants a new formal trial only when actual fits plus the additional meta-fit and changed number of refits fit the original limit, the weighted recipe beats the deployed recipe on each independent fold with pooled improvement at least 0.003, and it also beats the same-members equal vote in aggregate on these same folds. Otherwise preserve the actual autonomous delivery. No full-data training or external score is purchased by this diagnostic.
